#2653. Which team needs Tarik Skubal the most? Ranking the suitors for the best free agent available

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

As we emerge from the recent General Manager Meetings and move toward the expected Dec. 1 lockout of the players by MLB owners, we might see an accelerated pace of activity soon. The most tantalizing possibility is that ace and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, the undisputed top talent on the free agent market this winter, will sign before the sport shuts down for an indeterminate amount of time.

The decorated lefty, who soon turns 30, is our No. 1 free agent of the 2026-27 class, and it's not an especially close call. Here's part of our write-up:

"Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019. He showed few long-lasting effects from the NanoScope elbow surgery in May and remains a capital-A Ace with terrific surface stats and under-the-hood performance indicators. Skubal brings four swing-and-miss pitches to the table (four-seamer, changeup, slider, curveball), a near MLB-best ability to limit exit velocity, and elite strike-throwing ability (MLB's third-lowest walk rate since 2023). Build an ace starter in a lab and he would look a lot like Skubal. He'll play the entire 2027 season at age 30, and given the things teams can do with pitchers these days, Skubal figures to remain a frontline starter for most of a long-term contract. He's the only true balance-of-power player available in free agency this offseason. Skubal can swing a division race and a postseason series all by himself."

Will he set the record for the biggest contract ever signed by a pitcher? Will Skubal fetch the highest average annual salary for a pitcher? Will he top $400 million? Those are all reasonable questions to ask. First, though, there's a question to be asked about the teams that are already pursuing him the most vigorously. That question is, which team needs him the most? We're restricting our discussion to the five teams that have been most reliably linked to Skubal so far this offseason. We're already hearing reports of surprise teams, and it's always possible a surprise late bidder will enter the fray and even win his signature, but for now, these five clubs are the favorites. This, then, is an ordering of those teams based on which desperately needs a talent like Skubal in order to reach their goals in 2027 and beyond. Let's get to it, in order from "needs him the most" to "needs him but not as urgently as the teams ahead of them" …

The Cubs are in contention mode and in need of roster improvements if they're going to run down the world champion Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Central. The rotation is without question the most pressing need for Chicago. Shota Imanaga, Matthew Boyd, David Peterson, and deadline acquisition Clay Holmes are all free agents. Justin Steele hasn't taken the mound at the big-league level since early in the 2025 season thanks to UCL surgery and a halting recovery process. While he's expected to be ready for 2027, he's not exactly a known quantity right now. Young upsider Cade Horton may not be back until midseason after undergoing Tommy John surgery, and Ben Brown, who recently had neck surgery, may be on a similar timeline. So, yes, the Cubs need a lot of rotation help, and Skubal would give them the true frontline ace they'd lack even if everyone were healthy. Unfortunately for the Cubs fans, it sounds like the Ricketts aren't willing to be truly competitive for his services.

Coming off the grave disappointments of 2026, the Mets could certainly use a headline-grabbing addition to improve their chances in 2027 and inspire a surely disaffected fan base. Beyond that, the Mets need more starting pitching to accompany promising young Nolan McLean. Christian Scott seems like a lock, but he doesn't project as a frontliner. They have some depth options for the back end, but they need a true needle-mover like Skubal at the very front. That's especially the case in what figures to be a hotly competitive NL East in 2027. Thus far, David Stearns and owner Steve Cohen sound committed to making a good-faith run at Skubal.

The Padres have a lot of work to do if they're going to earn a fourth straight playoff appearance. Speaking of which, the rotation is crying out for help right about now. They lost Dylan Cease to free agency last winter, and this time Michael King may be bound elsewhere, too. The Pads declined their club option on Nick Pivetta, and while they hope to bring him back on more favorable terms, there's no guarantee they'll be able to do that. Yes, Joe Musgrove will be back, but how much can he give them and how effective will he be? They'll need even more help if Adrian Morejon, a lockdown bulk reliever and possible starter-conversion project, signs elsewhere. Skubal's made to order, and signing the top talent on the market would be a strong signal by new owners José E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones that the team's recent tradition of spending and contending won't be fading away.

The Dodgers self-evidently needed Skubal enough to acquire him from the Detroit Tigers leading up to the deadline and do so at significant cost. On paper, the Dodgers aren't as desperate for rotation help as the teams ahead of them on this list, but there's still a need. Yoshinobu Yamamoto is a certifiable ace, but behind him Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are established health and durability risks. Shohei Ohtani is something of an unknown, at least insofar as his pitching is concerned right now, and thus far Roki Sasaki and Emmet Sheehan have not proved worthy of being relied upon. One can squint and see the Dodgers' current championship window closing in the reasonably near future, which means that's all the more reason to push the chips in now. Retaining the elite services of Skubal would greatly aid the cause in 2027.

Eyeball a rotation that already includes Dylan Cease, José Soriano, and Trey Yesavage, and you might think it doesn't need much more. And maybe it doesn't. As a matter of principle, though, any team with contending aspirations should be interested in a top-shelf ace when he hits the market. The Jays, who in recent years have invested in the roster at commendable levels, are no doubt dreaming of a Skubal-Cease one-two punch that would be the envy of, oh, every other team in baseball. There's also depth to think about. In particular, Cody Ponce is a bit of an unknown coming off knee surgery that ended his 2026 season in the middle of his first start. Addressing the offense probably should be more of a priority for the Jays this winter, but, again, it's Tarik Skubal, and the likes of Tarik Skubal make any team better.

The upstart Chicago White Sox have added one of the game's hardest-throwing pitchers to their rotation. Chicago and righty Dustin May have agreed to a three-year contract worth $52.5 million, reports FanSided.

May, 29, split this past season between the St. Louis Cardinals and World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers. He threw a career-high 145 ⅔ innings with a 4.70 ERA, though the underlying numbers (3.63 FIP and 4.50 expected ERA) were more respectable. May's 96.9 mph average fastball velocity was 15th highest among the 141 pitchers with at least 100 innings in 2026.

Rotation help was a priority for a White Sox team that reached the postseason for the first time since 2021, but used openers and bullpen games regularly throughout the season. Only twice in seven postseason games did Chicago use a traditional starting pitcher. Here is the team's updated rotation depth chart:

Castillo struggled badly (30 runs in 31 innings) after coming over from the Seattle Mariners at the trade deadline, and finished the season on the injured list with a shoulder issue. His $22.75 million salary could land him in the rotation on Opening Day, though the White Sox have enough options to replace him should Castillo remain ineffective.

We ranked May as the offseason's 25th-best free agent, and the 11th-best starting pitcher. Here's a snippet of the write-up:

May turned only 29 in September and he's topped 130 innings in back-to-back years after throwing 101 innings total around injuries, including UCL surgery, from 2021-24. Even after the injuries, May still lives in the mid-to-upper-90s with his sinker, and pitch data models are fond of his sweeper and curveball. It is not the best sign, though, that the Brewers, who know pitching as well as any team, couldn't fully unlock May after making him their big deadline rotation addition. Still, the combination of age and high-octane stuff makes him a nice upside play ...

May made two starts and three relief appearances during Milwaukee's postseason run. If the White Sox opt to use bullpen games again next year, he is familiar and capable in that role. #2648. NASCAR Star Tries Bull Riding, Immediately Regrets It

NASCAR driver Noah Gragson thought trying bull riding would be an exciting change of pace. Instead, his trip to Davis Rodeo Ranch in North Carolina left him sore for an entire week. The Front Row Motorsports driver climbed aboard two bulls and quickly discovered that handling a race car and staying on a bucking bull require very different skills.

Speaking on This Cowboy Life podcast, Gragson described how the soreness began shortly after the experience. "I was pretty good there for a couple hours, and then I got to Olive Garden. We went to Olive Garden afterward in Salisbury, and my neck started getting kind of sore," he said.

Gragson said the discomfort worsened the following day. He struggled to raise his arm and described his shoulder as "killing me for the last week." The soreness also spread through his abdomen and groin, involving what he called "muscles I've never used before."

His introduction to bull riding involved two attempts. The first bull offered little resistance, but the second was considerably tougher. Gragson lasted approximately two seconds before getting thrown off. He also described being dashboarded during the experience. By the time he spoke on the podcast, about a week later, he said he was finally somewhat back to normal.

Nov 8, 2026; Homestead, Florida, USA; NASCAR Cup Series driver Noah Gragson (4) during the NASCAR Cup Series Championship Race at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images

Gragson even found an unusual way to get some relief during a visit to the Cosmopolitan Casino. He described receiving a massage while leaning over a blackjack table, paying $2 per minute for treatment focused on his neck and back. He credited the massage with helping his traps and neck finally feel better.

Gragson finally recovered enough to move freely again after a week of pain. His experience on the ranch in North Carolina remains a painful memory for the NASCAR star: "That was the craziest experience I've ever had."

#2647. NBA Rookie Rankings: Yaxel Lendeborg debuts at No. 1, Darryn Peterson making up ground in tight race

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

This season's NBA Rookie of the Year race has the potential to be one of the closest in league history. While there is no 65-game requirement to win the award — unlike MVP, Defensive Player of the Year and All-NBA honors — playing as many games as possible will be paramount this season in order to claim Rookie of the Year.

That's why Chicago Bulls forward Caleb Wilson faces an uphill climb to win the honor after fracturing his right hand earlier this month. Wilson is set to miss the next 3-5 weeks and will likely lose serious ground to others in his class. He currently has the sixth-best odds (+4000) on FanDuel Sportsbook to win Rookie of the Year.

During the first month of the season, three players have separated themselves at the top: Yaxel Lendeborg, Cameron Boozer, and Darius Acuff Jr. While it's not a guarantee one of those players wins it, if the season ended today, those would be the top vote-getters.

Darryn Peterson and AJ Dybantsa — the first two picks of the 2026 NBA Draft — have some ground to make up during the next four months to get back in the mix.

With the regular season almost a quarter of the way complete, let's dive into our first Rookie of the Year rankings. All odds via FanDuel.

With Steph Curry out, Lendeborg has continued to step up. The oldest player drafted in the first round is coming off a lackluster showing against the Spurs in the NBA Cup, but before that he had three straight games of 23+ points. He is shooting 48.6% from the field and 41.4% from 3. Lendeborg didn't start shooting 3s on a consistent basis until he got to Michigan last season, so knocking down that percentage on 5.4 attempts per night is a positive sign. Fourteen games into the season, Lendeborg is the favorite.

Boozer's raw stats aren't as good as Lendeborg's or even Acuff's, but his impact goes well beyond the box score. His feel for the game is elite for a 19-year-old. Boozer keeps getting better and better as a processor as he continues to log more minutes. The Grizzlies have been one of the league's surprising teams this season. Boozer deserves a ton of credit for that. He wins everywhere he goes, whether at the high school, college, or professional level.

Acuff just turned 20 last week. In 13 games as a teenager, he averaged 25.5 points per game and became the first teenager in NBA history to score at least 275 points and dish out 80 assists in his first 11 games. Acuff is a special offensive talent who is being asked to do more than any rookie in his class. Sacramento is a very bad basketball team, but Acuff makes the Kings somewhat fun to watch. That's a huge credit to him.

The Jazz have been decimated by injuries this season and are currently riding a 12-game losing streak. The one bright side amidst some very bad basketball is how good Peterson has been during that stretch. Peterson had a five-game stretch in which he scored 20 points in each game and shot the ball well from 3. Peterson is the future of Utah's franchise, so getting him as many reps as possible on and off the ball should be the priority.

Dybantsa, the No. 1 overall pick, is averaging 14 shot attempts per game during his first 10 appearances as a pro. He should be taking even more shots. The way the Wizards are using him is confusing at times. Dybantsa is in somewhat of a weird situation because of the Wizards' roster. Washington handed Trae Young a huge contract this offseason that is already aging poorly. Dybantsa should be the focus of the offense. He should be touching the ball and shooting it even more than he is already. I have been impressed with Dybantsa's defense this season.

#2646. Week 11 bold predictions: Fernando Mendoza upsets Broncos, Tony Pollard breaks Cowboys

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Almost anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 11 of the 2026 season showcased the limits of the league's parity.

In the Houston Texans' (4-6) 26-3 road win on the road over the torn-down Indianapolis Colts (3-8), three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor went for just 21 yards rushing on 11 carries. It marked an unfathomable 21 consecutive games without 100 yards rushing in a game, the worst drought of his career. Meanwhile, quarterback Daniel Jones just polished off his sixth straight game with an interception, the longest streak by a Colts player since Curtis Painter was filling in for an injured Peyton Manning in 2011.

Meanwhile, Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud threw two of his three touchdown passes for 20-plus air yards after having two combined in his first nine games of the 2026 season. Stroud's seven-game streak of multiple total touchdowns is now the longest in Texans history.

What surprises could occur across the rest of the NFL's Week 11 slate? Let's take a look at five bold predictions.

Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, made his debut as an NFL starting quarterback against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 10. That made Mendoza the first No. 1 overall pick in NFL history to make his first career start against the defending Super Bowl champion, per CBS Sports Research. He held his own, completing 17 of his 29 throws for 143 yards while also adding 22 yards and a rushing touchdown on six carries. Despite being sacked six times, Mendoza and the Raiders only lost by eight points, 21-13.

After adjusting to the pace of the NFL game against the Seahawks, Mendoza and the Raiders will head to Empower Field at Mile High Stadium in Denver and emerge victorious against the Broncos. Denver quarterback Bo Nix doesn't scare any defense, ranking last in the league in air yards per pass attempt (5.6). For whatever reason, he can't or won't pull the trigger on throws down the field. Five-time Pro Bowl Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby will do enough to spook Nix while Mendoza helps Las Vegas' offense score just enough points for the 10.5-point underdogs, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, to emerge victorious on Sunday.

Tony Pollard is ascending to new heights at the age of 29 and in the final year of his three-year, $21.75 million contract with the Tennessee Titans. Across his last three games, Pollard has produced 279 yards rushing, 112 yards receiving and six total touchdowns. Even though the Titans had a Week 9 bye, Pollard still ranks in the top 10 in rushing yards, rushing touchdowns, receiving touchdowns and total touchdowns by a running back since Week 7. His five rushing touchdowns are tied for the most in the NFL in this span with Bucky Irving, and his six scrimmage touchdowns in this stretch are tied for the most in the league with Christian McCaffrey.

Pollard now has his sights set on scoring a touchdown in four consecutive games for the first time in his eight-season NFL career. And just in time for his first matchup with the Dallas Cowboys, the team that drafted him in the fourth round of the 2019 NFL Draft and the team he called home for his first five seasons. His homecoming on Sunday at AT&T Stadium will mark Pollard's first career game against the Cowboys, and he'll have a special day against a Dallas defense that is in total disarray after the half-firing of first-time defensive coordinator Christian Parker on Wednesday. Parker retains his title as defensive coordinator, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer stripped him of defensive play-calling duties and gave them to senior assistant Mike Pettine, a 60-year-old who was retired and vacationing in Italy just a few months ago. Pettine last worked as a defensive play-caller in the NFL in 2020, his final season as the defensive coordinator of the Green Bay Packers.

Pollard will join Jahmyr Gibbs (twice this season), Bijan Robinson (Week 3 at the Green Bay Packers) and McCaffrey (Week 10 at the Cowboys) as just the fourth player in the entire league this season with 200-plus scrimmage yards and multiple touchdowns in a game on Sunday against his old friends.

Detroit Lions Pro Bowl running back Jahmyr Gibbs decimated the New England Patriots for 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing yards on 22 carries plus 99 yards on seven catches), the most in a game by any player this season. He also added two rushing touchdowns in the Lions' 35-10 stomping of the Patriots in Munich, Germany. What can the league's rushing yards (1,000), scrimmage yards (1,384) and scrimmage touchdowns (13) leader do for Week 11 as an encore against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the NFL's No. 1 run defense?

The Bucs  are giving up just 79.2 rushing yards per game allowed. But Gibbs will steamroll Buccaneers Pro Bowl defensive tackle Vita Vea and Co. for 120 yards rushing, something that hasn't been done to Tampa Bay since TreVeyon Henderson did so in Week 10 of last season. Do you know who produced the next-most-recent occurrence against the Buccaneers? That's right, it was Gibbs in Week 7 of the 2025 season when he went off for 136 yards rushing and two touchdowns on 17 carries in a 24-9 victory. He'll go over 120 again against the NFL's best run defense on Sunday.

The Miami Dolphins head up north to Buffalo to face the 8-1 Bills, the AFC's No. 1 seed, as 16.5-point underdogs per DraftKings Sportsbook. Essentially, the expectation is for the Dolphins to lose by three scores. It's understandable to see why. Bills quarterback Josh Allen has the most total touchdowns in a player's first 10 seasons (325) despite 2026 being just his ninth NFL season. Allen alone has more career playoff touchdowns (39) than Miami's active roster (38) does in the regular season. The Dolphins active roster's 38 combined career touchdowns are the fewest in the NFL by any team's active roster by nearly 50 touchdowns — the Arizona Cardinals are the next-lowest with 85.

Buffalo is tied for the best record in the NFL along with the San Francisco 49ers at 8-1, while Miami is tied for the worst record at 1-8 with the Titans and the Los Angeles Chargers. However, the Dolphins will lose by only one score on Sunday.

How is this possible? Well, the Bills have outscored their opponents 90-28 in their last three games while facing five backup quarterbacks: Tyler Huntley, Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz, Max Brosmer and Cade Klubnik. Yes, the Dolphins are starting one too — 2025 sixth-round pick Kyle McCord — with Malik Willis sidelined, but McCord had a decent debut at theIndianapolis Colts in Week 10. He threw for 209 yards, the second most in an NFL debut in Dolphins history, on 17-of-32 passing with a rushing touchdown and one lost fumble. Rookie third-round wide receiver Caleb Douglas' 367 yards receiving in six games is the most in a player's first six career games in Dolphins history.

No team in the last 20 years has seen a higher rate of their snaps (28.8%) go to rookies than the 2026 Dolphins have. They don't know what they don't know. That's why they're going to lose by just one possession against the mighty Bills in Buffalo in Week 11.

Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams returns from a Week 10 bye out for blood after throwing four interceptions in Week 9 against the Buccaneers. That snapped his 36-game streak without multiple interceptions, the fourth-longest streak by a starting quarterback since 1950. Williams will be itching to go deep downfield to wide receivers Luther Burden and Rome Odunze to atone for his sloppy play in the last time out.

Williams' problem is that he is facing one of the best pass-rushing teammate duos in football against the New Orleans Saints. Saints edge rushers Carl Granderson (8.5 sacks, tied for the second most in the NFL) and Chase Young (8.0 sacks, tied for the fourth-most) have combined for 16.5 sacks, tied for the most of any teammate pass rush duo this season along with the Minnesota Vikings' Andrew Van Ginkel (8.5) and Dallas Turner (8.0).

The Saints' defense as a whole hasn't been stellar this season, profiling as the league's No. 25 scoring defense (26.2 points per game allowed), but they'll combine to sack Williams a season-high five times on Sunday. Williams' 3.35-second average time to throw is the longest in the NFL among the league's 31 qualified quarterbacks, which will doom him against Granderson, Young and the New Orleans defense.

#2644. Abilene Wylie falls to Montgomery Lake Creek in 5A DII UIL Volleyball State Championship

The Abilene Wylie Lady Bulldogs made their return to the UIL Volleyball State Championships on Saturday morning, Nov. 21, at the Curtis Calwell Center in Garland, Texas.

The Lady Bulldogs – who were making their first appearance in a UIL Volleyball State Championship game since beating La Grange for the 3A state title in 2012 – found themselves locked in a fiercely competitive match against the Montgomery Lake Creek Lady Lions.

What began as a back-and-forth battle, though, gradually slipped away from Wylie, which fell in straight sets to Lake Creek 3-0 (25-19, 28-26, 25-14) in the Class 5A Division II UIL Volleyball State Championship match.

The loss ends a remarkable postseason run by the Lady Bulldogs that included straight-set victories over West Texas powers Wolfforth Frenship and El Paso Del Valle, as well as several signature wins against DFW-area powerhouse programs Eagle Mountain, Argyle and Colleyville Heritage in the later rounds of the UIL Playoffs.

Senior outside hitter Haddie Mock – a Stephen F. Austin commit – and senior middle blocker Jenna Stricklin set the tone for the Wylie defensively and led the Lady Bulldogs offensively along the net.

Mock tallied seven kills, six blocks and one dig, while Stricklin recorded seven kills, five digs and two blocks.

Junior outside hitter Kiki Bolden and junior defensive specialist Morgan Bearden and Annalise Loudermilk anchored Abilene Wylie's back-line defense and were instrumental in extending several key rallies.

Bolden – Wylie's team captain – logged 17 digs, five kills, three blocks and one assist. Loudermilk posted a team-leading 19 assists with two digs, two kills and two blocks, while Bearden finished with a team-high 18 digs and three assists.

Lake Creek junior Blaire Sexton was named MVP of the 5A DII UIL Volleyball State Championship match after racking up 15 kills, 10 doubles and four aces.

Montgomery Lake Creek (44-10) secured its first UIL Volleyball State Championship in school history during the Lady Lions' first trip to the state tournament since 2022.

Abilene Wylie, meanwhile, closes out its best season in program history at 39-5 overall with the Lady Bulldogs finishing their season in the state tournament for just the fourth time in school history and the first time in 14 years.

#2643. MLB rumors: Mets meet with Tarik Skubal, Red Sox getting calls for multiple players, plus Cubs, Red Sox, more

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The annual GM Meetings came and went last week with two significant transactions. The Braves signed reliever Evan Phillips (three years and $35 million) and the Red Sox signed slugger Jake Bauers (four years and $58 million). Bauers will give Boston some desperately needed home run power. Phillips will pair with Robert Suarez in the late innings for Atlanta.

Otherwise, we're still waiting on the winter's first true blockbuster, and the clock is ticking with a lockout expected upon the collective bargaining agreement's expiration at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Tuesday's hot stove happenings.

Teams are calling the Rangers about left-hander MacKenzie Gore, who is a year away from free agency, according to The Athletic. There is some reluctance to trade for players with only one year of control because games could be lost to a work stoppage next year, but pitching is so in-demand that at least some clubs are exploring a deal for Gore.

Now 27, Gore is one of only six pitchers to make at least 30 starts in each of the last three years. His under-the-hood numbers (3.87 FIP and 4.19 expected ERA) were much better than his 4.58 actual ERA, plus he has long been considered to have untapped upside. Gore will give you innings, at minimum, and there's a chance his best days are ahead of him.

The Red Sox are exploring the trade market for righties Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck, and Johan Oviedo, according to WEEI. They are also believed to be preparing to trade Jarren Duran, reports MassLive.com. Duran is a potential non-tender candidate if the Red Sox are unable to find a trade partner prior to Friday's deadline. The Mariners and Phillies are among the teams that are "poking around."

Crawford, Houck, and Ovideo all missed significant time with injuries in 2026 (Crawford has not appeared in an MLB game since 2024) and are far down Boston's rotation depth chart. Duran has been pushed out of the everyday lineup by the recent Jake Bauers signing. Exploring trades for these four players in a seller's market is a sensible approach.

The Mets had an in-person meeting with top-ranked free agent Tarik Skubal on Monday, reports the New York Post. Owner Steve Cohen and president of baseball operations David Stearns were among those in attendance, according to SNY. Skubal and agent Scott Boras will meet with the Blue Jays, Dodgers, Padres, and potentially two other teams in the coming days.

Skubal is expected to sign before the lockout and is therefore working on a tight schedule, much tighter than usual for top Boras clients. Nolan McLean and Christian Scott give the Mets two promising young arms to build around, but they need to improve the rotation around them, and Skubal would give the club a no-doubt ace to lead the pitching staff.

The pitching-needy Cubs have shown interest in free agent lefty Trevor Rogers, reports The Athletic. Chicago needs multiple starters this offseason and has cast a wide net in their search. Justin Steele (UCL) and Ben Brown (neck), ostensibly the Cubs' No. 1 and 2 starters, are both recovering from surgeries, and Brown is expected to miss the start of 2027.

We ranked Rogers as the third-best free agent available this offseason because he is very good as is, and because he'll make analytical models hum with the quality of his arsenal and strike-throwing. Nine pitchers made at least nine starts for the Cubs in 2026 and only two -- Javier Assad and Edward Cabrera -- currently remain under contract/team control.

The AL East rival Orioles and Yankees are among the teams with interest in free agent slugger Randy Arozarena, according to the Baltimore Banner and New York Post. The O's also have some interest in re-signing Luis Robert Jr. Other than Dylan Beavers and maybe Tyler O'Neill, Baltimore's outfield is wide open right now. They have DH at-bats available too.

It is likely the Yankees checked in on Arozarena out of due diligence more than serious interest. His righty bat would help their lefty-heavy lineup, though he would be a clunky roster fit as a corner outfielder who really needs to DH on a team that already has plenty of corner outfielders who really need to DH. If Arozarena's market is slow to develop, perhaps New York would pounce.

Teams around the league believe the Rockies are more open to trading All-Star catcher Hunter Goodman now than they were at the trade deadline, reports MLB Network. Colorado is said to have set a very high asking price for Goodman, who in 2026 became just the tenth primary catcher with a 40-homer season. He hit more homers on the road (25) than at Coors Field (16) too.

Ryan Jeffers and Carson Kelly represent viable free agent alternatives to Goodman as right-handed offense-first catchers, though Goodman is several years younger than both and will have a lower salary the next three years through arbitration. Teams will likely feel more confident in Goodman holding his production for another few years than Jeffers and Kelly.

#2642. LeBron James denies report that he asked 76ers for 'patience' with scoring numbers at career low

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Philadelphia 76ers are off to a fantastic start to the 2026-27 season at 12-3, good for first in the Eastern Conference, and perhaps most encouraging for the Sixers is that they're winning without looking like a team playing at its absolute peak.

After a huge offseason adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, the Sixers still look like a team figuring out how best to work together, but when it comes time in the fourth quarter to find a way to win, they manage to get the job done. Tyrese Maxey is leading the way with Brown quickly finding his rhythm, but James and Joel Embiid in particular still seem to be feeling it out early in the season.

James, who has never averaged less than 20.9 points per game in his previous 23 seasons, is averaging just 15.1 points per game and his 44.3/22.5/71.7 shooting splits are all career lows or close to it. As James figures things out, ESPN reported that a Sixers source claimed James "asked coaches to be patient with him as he expects to find his rhythm and get his conditioning in line by December as he ramps up."

That report hit social media and caught James' attention, with the 41-year-old star denying ever saying that.

ESPN didn't report a direct quote from James, and it's very possible the Sixers source offered an anecdote that paraphrased James and used the word patience when James never did. That then ended up on a social media graphic and prompted James to shoot it down.

What's fascinating here is it's not a scathing report or even anything particularly juicy. James is struggling with his shot early in the year and seems to be figuring out exactly where he fits in the offense alongside Maxey, Brown and Embiid as a scorer. He's still doing plenty of things well -- including leading the team with 6.9 assists per game and just took over third all-time in assists in NBA history -- and the Sixers are still winning even with James ice cold with his jumper, which history suggests will turn around at some point.

Patience would be prudent from the Sixers with James, whether he wants to use that word or not, and it seems like a matter of when, not if, he gets shots to start falling and the Philly offense becomes even more dynamic.

#2641. NFL exploring possibility of implementing new travel rules for international games

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

With the NFL's uptick in international games over the last few years, there's no rule requiring a team to arrive in a foreign city by a certain date before a game, but that could change. That could change soon.

The NFL is currently exploring a new travel policy that would require each team to spend a minimum number of nights in an international city. In an interview this week with The Athletic, NFL executive VP of club business Peter O'Reilly confirmed that a change could be coming.

"Currently, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club," O'Reilly said. "It is something that we'll consider moving forward on: Do we put some minimum nights in a market in there? It's something we'll look at."

It's no surprise the NFL is thinking hard about this topic, especially after what happened in Week 1 during the league's first regular-season game in Australia between the 49ers and the Rams. The 49ers decided to fly out a full week before the game so they could acclimate to the 17-hour time difference. Leaving early also allowed the team to fully immerse themselves in Australian culture.

On the other hand, the Rams infamously didn't arrive until the last minute: They landed in Melbourne at about 7 a.m. ET on Thursday morning, leaving them less than 30 hours until their game with the 49ers kicked off.

The Rams traveled late so that their players wouldn't have to adjust to Australian time, but the plan backfired. The Rams looked slow and tired during a 27-7 loss.

If the NFL does implement a minimum-night rule, it likely won't be anything dramatic. The rule that would make the most sense is having teams arrive at least two nights in advance. For a game in Europe, that would mean a team would have to leave Thursday night to arrive Friday.

That exact travel plan was not only popular this year, but also successful. In fact, teams traveling to Europe went 4-0 this year when arriving on Friday. The Steelers, Texans, Colts, and Jaguars (for their first London game) all arrived Friday morning for their international game, and all four teams won. It's hard to imagine the NFL creating a rule to eliminate something that's working well for teams, so if the league implements a new travel policy, it likely won't be a massive change.

Since international play started in 2007, there are only three instances of a team showing up the day before a game in a city at least five time zones away, and the Rams were involved in two of them. The Rams arrived on Saturday in London for a 35-7 blowout win over the Jaguars in 2025, which is why they likely felt good about arriving the day before the game in Australia this year. The Eagles ended up copying the Rams' strategy for their game in London this year, arriving on Saturday for their matchup against the Jags, which ended up being a dramatic 19-17 loss.

There were a total of nine international games this year, and the final one will be played in Mexico City on Sunday night between the Vikings and the 49ers. If the NFL does implement a new travel policy, it will be interesting to see whether it includes games like this that are geographically closer to the United States. The Vikings are flying down to the game on Saturday because the flight from Minnesota to Mexico City is only about 4.5 hours and there's no time zone change, so it's not necessarily a reason to travel early (The stadium in Mexico City does have an altitude of 7,350 feet, so it could make sense to travel early to get acclimated to that, but the Vikings decided not to go that route).

Under the current CBA, the NFL is allowed to schedule up to 10 international games for 2027, and if the league hits that number, it will certainly be interesting to see if a new travel policy is in place for next season.

#2639. Jake Bauers signs four-year, $58 million deal with Red Sox after helping lead Brewers to World Series

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Boston Red Sox have made the offseason's first major free agent signing. The Red Sox and first baseman Jake Bauers have agreed to a four-year contract worth a reported $58 million, the team announced on Tuesday.

Bauers, 31, broke out with the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers this past season, authoring a .266/.389/.484 batting line with 26 home runs that more than doubled his previous career high (12). He was named the NLCS MVP during Milwaukee's title run thanks to a 4 for 14 (.286) effort. Bauers drove in seven runs in the four-game sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers.

The Red Sox desperately needed a power bat and certainly added one with Bauers. Their 163 home runs this past season were the fifth fewest in baseball and three players -- Wilyer Abreu, Willson Contreras and Jarren Duran -- accounted for 71 of those 163 home runs. Boston's lineup figures to look something like this with Bauers now added:

That leaves Duran without a full-time position and makes a trade or even a non-tender more likely. Franklin Arias, one of the very best prospects in the minors, could debut early next season and wrestle the shortstop job away from Story. POBO Craig Breslow recently said Story is not locked in as the team's starting shortstop.

We ranked Bauers as the 12th-best free agent available this offseason, and the seventh-best position player free agent. Here's our write-up:

Rake Bauers (finally) lived up to the nickname this year and carried it over into the postseason, particularly during the NLCS. Long an exit velocity and hard-hit rate darling, Bauers fully tapped into his power in 2026 thanks to a more open stance and moving back in the box and further off the plate. That allowed him to see the ball better and get his bat into the hitting position on time more consistently. I'm not 100% sold on those adjustments solving his career-long issues with lefties, though at least there is a tangible reason to believe in his great left-on-left performance this season. Bauers can be an adventure in the field (he has played outfield in the past) and he just turned 31. A few teams will look for the next Jake Bauers rather than pay the actual Jake Bauers.

The Brewers tendered Bauers the $23.15 million qualifying offer and will receive a 2027 compensation draft pick after the first round because the contract exceeds $50 million. Because they paid the competitive balance tax, the Red Sox will forfeit their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in bonus pool money for the 2027 international signing period, to sign Bauers.

Milwaukee could turn to Tyler Black and Andrew Vaughn at first base next season. Andrew Fischer, the No. 20 overall pick in the 2025 draft, slugged 48 home runs in the minors this summer and reached Double-A. He is the long-term solution at first base but is likely a year away from the big leagues. The Brewers could bring in a stopgap first baseman if they're not sold on Black.

The Red Sox went 87-75 this past season and were the second wild card team. They were swept by the rival New York Yankees in the Wild Card Series and scored only two runs in the two games.

#2638. NBA MVP Rankings: Luka Dončić, Victor Wembanyama in a two-horse race; Stephen Curry's absence speaks volumes

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

We're nearly a month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and while some people say it's too early to start talking about MVP, we are not among those people.

Right now, it's a clear two-horse race: Luka Doncic or Victor Wembanyama? There is a real split on this. Here's where I stand as of Tuesday, Nov. 17.

The Luka Dončić we're watching right now isn't just the best offensive player in the world. He might be the best in history. Nobody has ever put up anything close to the numbers he is charting at the moment: 39 points per game with seven assists, seven boards, nearly two steals and a positively scorching 66.0 TS%, the latter being a number even the great Stephen Curry has only bested twice in his career.

It's early, sure. Dončić isn't likely to keep making 3s at this rate for an entire season, and indeed we've seen some slippage of late (35% over his last four, if you really want to split hairs), but his volume remains, with 4.5 makes a night over that stretch. Dončić remains on track to break Curry's single-season record of 402 3-pointers, and he's done more off-ball shooting than in the past.

Throw in more transition production and a 53% midrange conversion rate, per Cleaning The Glass, and you're seeing a more diverse scorer, which is to say this isn't just a guy who has started off hot on his step-back 3s (though this is a major factor, too, of course), but a guy piercing defenses from more spots with different shots. If Dončić could actually be any harder to guard than he has been in the past, we're seeing it this season.

He's also defending. His 23 steals rank sixth league-wide. Only two players have recovered more defensive loose balls than his eight. Only one has taken more charges than his four. With Dončić as the primary defender, shooters are converting just 36.7% of their shots against a 45.1 expected FG%; that minus-8.6 is the fourth-largest discrepancy among all players who've contested at least 150 shots.

Most importantly, the Lakers are 12-2 and tied with the Spurs atop the Western Conference. The Lakers rank as the league's top offense with a rating that balloons to 129.2 points per 100 possessions (which would be an NBA record by a long shot) with Dončić on, and a net rating, as illustrated below, that falls off a cliff when he sits.

Look, if you have Wembanyama ahead of Dončić in the MVP race a month into the season, nobody is going to argue much with you. The oddsmakers slightly favor Wembanyama (+110 at FanDuel; Dončić is +140), who, as you'll see below, has what would qualify as a potentially unanimous case in most years. But this isn't most years. We got a dude averaging nearly 40 points for a No. 1 seed that nobody expected to be a No. 1 seed. Until one of those things changes, it's hard for me to go against Dončić.

If you think Dončić's plus-35.5 on/off split (it's actually plus-32.2 without filtering for garbage time) is crazy, have a look at Wembanyama's number.

Victor Wembanyama's impact this season has been another level. Spurs are +42.6 points per 100 possessions with Wemby on the court than off it, according to @cleantheglass. Small sample but other-worldly. Lakers star Luka Dončić is at +35.5 pts/100 poss.Both numbers are better… pic.twitter.com/0GJCFFmZ5K

Yes, you're reading that right. The Spurs, for all their supportive talent, fall by 42.6 points per 100 possessions when Wembanyama leaves the court (plus-29.2 on vs. minus-13.3 off), per Cleaning the Glass. By comparison, the best on/off split that Nikola Jokić has ever recorded is plus-24.8. Curry's best is plus-21.3. LeBron James' is plus-17.8. Go down that list and look at the most impactful on-off splits those guys have ever posted. Wembanyama is in another galaxy.

And it's important to note that Wembanyama plays on a great team, as all these guys in the graphic have. The fact that there is still so much difference between when Wembanyama is on the court and when he isn't, even in a small sample, is honestly difficult to comprehend. San Antonio's three-guard lineup was supposed to be an experiment, but it's hard to know if Dylan Harper, De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle truly optimize one another or if Wembanyama is enough to make any lineup dominant in spite of traditional issues (like none of those three being a true shooter).

Wembanyama is the best defensive player on the planet by an immeasurable amount. Even the stats don't do it justice. He's on pace for north of 350 blocks, a number only four players (Elmore Smith, Mark Eaton, Manute Bol and Hakeem Olajuwon) have eclipsed since blocks became an official stat in 1973, and still it's just as much, if not more, about the shots he deters scorers from even attempting.

And why would they? Scorers are making just 33.6% of their shots when Wembanyama is the nearest defender, a 17% drop from their expected 50.4%. That also leads the league among all players who've defended at least 120 shots, and again, it fails to fully capture his defensive dominance.

The fact that we've gotten this far without talking about Wembanyama's offense, as if it's a mere afterthought for a guy to be averaging 28.6 points and 11.6 rebounds in under 30 minutes a night. Wembanyama is figuring out his hot spots, prioritizing closer-to-the-basket positioning where he is a skyscraper among regular NBA buildings. He's taking two more paint shots per game than he did last season; 43% of his shots are coming from inside four feet, per Cleaning the Glass, up from 38% last season, and his 4.6 dunks per game (up from 2.7 last year) have him on pace to shatter Rudy Gobert's single-season record of 306.

If I had to guess, Wembanyama's production is more sustainable than Dončić's. It's hard to imagine Dončić not hitting a rough patch from 3, and he's almost certainly not going to keep scoring 39 points per game. He'll be over 35 points per game when everything is said and done because that's what the Lakers need from him, but there's a burnout factor while Wembanyama is kind of cruising to these numbers, and the defensive impact is as natural as breathing. My gut says Wembanyama will be a clearer MVP favorite by Christmas.

Assuming Dončić and Wembanyama each get to the mandated 65 games, everyone else is playing for third place at the moment. Which is crazy given the seasons some of the following names are having.

One of two players averaging at least 22 points, nine rebounds and seven assists, and the only player to be leading his team in all three categories. The Rockets are 11-4 with the No. 2 offense and Sengun is the center of it all.

Tatum is averaging his normal 26.5 points per game. The shooting efficiency still hasn't come around, but he is an absolute quarterback on this Celtics team. He draws the doubles, and his 35.1% assist rate, per CTG, is a career high by a mile. The Celtics, for my money, are the best team in the East.

Cunningham is, once again, doing everything for the Pistons, who have been without Jalen Duren for all but the first four games and are still a top-three East seed. The 3-point shooting is down, but that's splitting hairs. This guy is shot-creating machine and, as forceful as he plays, he makes it look as smooth as anyone in the league.

Here come the Heat, who have won five straight games, with the last three wins coming over the Cavaliers, Pistons and Rockets. Antetokounmpo is averaging 28.3/12.5/5.2 with 1.3 blocks per game on 60% shooting. He's on fire from the midrange as the Heat are exploiting the soft spots in all the drop coverage they're facing.

Gilgeous-Alexander has so much on his plate that it actually creates a clearer path to a third straight MVP if he can somehow lift Oklahoma City above all these injuries. He's trying. The Thunder are 9-5 and he's getting his 30.9 points per game, but his 58.7 true-shooting is down considerably, which makes sense as he has to force tougher shots now with fewer weapons around him.

Curry's value can perhaps be felt most in his absence. The Warriors have lost three straight since he went out with a torn oblique, the last two by 59 points. The Warriors have outscored opponents by 13.5 points per 100 possessions with Curry on the floor this season and have been outscored by 8.3 points per 100 possessions without him. Along with Yaxel Lendeborg, who's being asked as a rookie to carry an impossibly heavy weight without Curry, Curry remains the only real lifeblood of a team that is still shockingly lifeless without him.

#2637. Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs laying early foundation for one of the best running back careers ever

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

For the first three years of his NFL career, Detroit Lions three-time Pro Bowl running back Jahmyr Gibbs was known as part of one of the NFL's best running back tandems, the "Sonic" in the Lions' "Sonic and Knuckles" duo with David Montgomery. Today, Gibbs is showing that, as a solo act, not only can he can be the NFL's No. 1 back, but he's also laying the early groundwork to become one of the greatest running backs of all time.

Yes, that sounds hyperbolic, but Gibbs' production is at all-time levels through three-and-a-half seasons. On an international stage in Week 10, he erupted for 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing yards on 22 carries plus 99 yards on 7 catches), the most in a game by any player this season, and 2 rushing touchdowns in the Lions' 35-10 stomping of the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. An outing like that reshuffles some NFL record boards.

Just halfway through his fourth season, Gibbs passed Pro Football Hall of Famer Terrell Davis (61 touchdowns in his first four seasons) for the most touchdowns in a player's first four seasons in NFL history (62 and counting). Gibbs is also now the first player in NFL history with 1,000 rushing yards (exactly 1,000) and 350 receiving yards (384) in a player's first nine games of a season. With an NFL-best 1,384 yards from scrimmage and a league-high13 scrimmage touchdowns in nine games, Gibbs is on pace for an NFL single-season record: 2,614 yards from scrimmage, which would smash current record holder Chris Johnson's 2,509 from the 2009 season.

All of those feats are jaw-dropping on their own, but together they paint an all-time picture. What is perhaps most amazing about Gibbs is how consistently excellent he is, to the point that the football world is somewhat numb to his greatness. Producing 150-plus rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in a game is outstanding. Six players have produced such a game this season, but five of the six have done so no more than twice. Then there is Gibbs, who has done so four times in Detroit's first nine games, making him just the fourth player in NFL history to do so. The other three are a who's who of Hall of Fame running backs: Jim Brown (1958, 1963), O.J. Simpson (1974, 1975) and Emmitt Smith (1995).

Now, some people might feel Gibbs' historic start to his NFL career is amplified by a talent offensive ecosystem that has a five-time Pro Bowler at quarterback, Jared Goff, a four-time Pro Bowler at wide receiver (Amon-Ra St. Brown), a Pro Bowl tight end (Sam LaPorta), a four-time Pro Bowl offensive tackle (Penei Sewell), and a speedster No. 2 wide receiver (Jameson Williams). However, Gibbs and his consistent excellence power everything else in the Motor City team's offense. He ranks seventh in the league in yards before contact per rush (1.57) and eighth in yards after contact per rush (3.5) this season.

Among the 27 players with at least 100 carries in 2026, Gibbs' 29.1% tackles-avoided rate is the second-best in the league, behind only Kenneth Walker III's 32.1% rate. Since Next Gen Stats began tracking explosive runs (runs of 10 or more yards) in 2016, no running back has produced more through the first 10 weeks of a season than Gibbs' 34. Prime Ezekiel Elliott in his rookie year with the Dallas Cowboys in 2016 is the closest player in this span with 29. Gibbs isn't just a cog in the Lions' machine: his juice powers the rest of the machine.

Here's the cherry on top. Not even through his fourth NFL season, Gibbs has more games (two) with 250-plus scrimmage yards and multiple touchdowns in his 58-game career than Barry Sanders, the running back many believe is the best pure runner ever, did in his 10-season, 153-game career.

Week 11 gives Gibbs a chance to deliver an all-time encore performance in a matchup against Pro Bowl defensive tackle Vita Vea and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the No. 1 run defense in the NFL (79.2 rushing yards per game allowed) this season. Get your popcorn ready as Gibbs continues to build a strong case for being the league's most productive running back ever.

#2635. Yankees' David Bednar, Twins' Ryan Jeffers accept qualifying offer, six others reject $23.15 million QO

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Two players have accepted this year's one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer prior to Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET. deadline, and six others have declined the QO. David Bednar (Yankees) and Ryan Jeffers (Twins) are returning to their teams, for the 2027 season, while Randy Arozarena (Mariners),  Brandon Lowe (Pirates), Adrian Morejon (Padres), Trevor Rogers (Orioles), and Seiya Suzuki (Cubs) are all hitting the market.

An eighth free agent, Jake Bauers, also received the QO. He agreed to a four-year, $58 million contract with the Red Sox this past weekend. Effectively, Bauers declined the QO. Because they paid CBT in 2026, the Red Sox will surrender their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in 2027 international bonus pool money, to sign Bauers. The Brewers, as a revenue-sharing receiver, will receive a compensation draft pick after the first round because the contract exceeds $50 million.

The five unsigned free agents who rejected the QO are now tied to draft pick compensation. Their former teams will receive a draft pick if they sign elsewhere, and their new teams will be docked a draft pick and potentially international bonus pool money to sign them. The exact compensation depends on the team's revenue sharing and competitive balance tax (CBT) status.

Here is draft pick compensation the former teams will receive if the seven qualified free agents change teams:

Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M

Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M

Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M

CBT payors, like the Red Sox, will forfeit their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in 2027 international bonus pool money, to sign a qualified free agent. Teams that receive revenue sharing will surrender their third-highest 2027 draft pick. All other teams will surrender their second-highest 2027 draft pick and $500,000 in 2027 international bonus pool money.

It must be noted that declining the QO does not mean the free agent can not return to his former team. The two sides could still work out a contract of any size and any length, including one worth less than QO, though that is very unlikely. Zac Gallen, Michael King, and Kyle Schwarber rejected the QO last offseason and then later re-signed with their teams.

Free agents must meet certain criteria to be eligible for the QO. Players cannot have received the QO previously and they must have spent the most recent season with one team, meaning anyone traded in-season is ineligible. The Dodgers could not give Tarik Skubal, far and away the offseason's best free agent, the QO following his midseason acquisition.

The QO is set at the average of the top 125 salaries in the most recent season and that is salaries only, not total compensation. For example, the Yankees paid Cody Bellinger a $20 million signing bonus and a $32.5 million salary in 2026. Only the $32.5 million counts toward the QO calculation. This QO was worth a record $23.15 million this winter.

The current QO system replaced the old free-agent arbitration system in 2012 and will remain in effect this offseason. The upcoming collective bargaining agreement could change the QO system, if not eliminate it entirely. Entering the offseason, just 18 of the 157 free agents to receive the QO accepted it. That count is now at 20 of 165.

One of the more effective closers in baseball last season, Bednar closed down 35 of 39 save chances with a 2.47 ERA, 1.04 WHIP and 76 strikeouts in 69 ⅓ innings. Having him back on board means the Yankees don't need to find a new closer and can look instead to shore up the bridge to the ninth as needed.

There had been talk that Jeffers wanted to stay with the Twins but that he'd decline the QO and then negotiate a long-term deal. There's still room to reach an extension, of course, but he now doesn't have any leverage from outside offers. It's a big win for the Twins, with Jeffers resuming his role as the everyday catcher and Victor Caratini serving as the primary backup.

Jeffers hit .256/.353/.461 (127 OPS+) with 14 homers and 56 RBI is only 92 games last season. He's been one of the most productive offensive catchers in baseball over the course of the last four seasons, when healthy.
